name: Penske Automotive Group, Inc.
sector: Consumer Discretionary / Automotive & commercial truck retail
moat_justification: Franchise-protected local dealership territories, scale as the second-largest US franchised dealer group, premium/luxury brand mix and a high-margin recurring service & parts business give a moderate moat; ROIC was 17.0-19.6% in 2022-23 but has fallen to 12.4% in FY2025 (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) and gross margin has eased from 17.4% to 16.4%, while powerful OEMs control allocations and brand standards, margins are thin (~4% operating) and the business is deeply cyclical — so 5/10, not higher.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.8%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 3.7x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Solid franchised dealer group, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% on current TTM numbers (6.5% weighted IRR, IV@15% $68.47 vs $212.42 price; hurdle price for 15% is $68.47); the price sits at the $210 Penske Corp/Mitsui take-private proposal, i.e. it is a control/deal price, not standalone owner's-earnings value.
moat_for: State franchise laws create protected local dealership territories
Scale: second-largest US franchised dealer group, leverage in OEM allocations and acquisitions
Premium/luxury brand mix with better margins than volume peers
Service & parts: recurring, ~55-60% gross-margin revenue that cushions vehicle-sale cyclicality (Q2 2026 same-store service & parts revenue +2%, gross margin +80bp to 59.5%)
Diversification beyond US retail autos: Premier Truck Group (commercial trucks), Australia/UK operations and the Penske Transportation Solutions equity stake
moat_against: OEMs hold the power: they control production, allocations, franchise size/location and brand standards
Thin economics: blended gross margin 16.4% in FY2025 (17.4% in 2021-22), operating margin only 4.03%
ROIC falling through the cycle: 19.6% (2022) -> 17.0% -> 14.4% -> 12.4% (2025) per fundamentals.json
Cyclical vehicle demand, affordability and interest-rate exposure; new-vehicle GPU fell 10.4% YoY in Q2 2026
Direct-to-consumer OEM models (Tesla and others) threaten the franchise model long term; intense rivalry from AutoNation, Lithia and private dealers
